incident-bot: :rotating_light: HOSTED-API (us-east-1) ALERT — sustained request queue growth, p99 latency > 25s, autoscaler failing to provision GPUs. Auto-page to SRE and Infra.
Maya R: I'm awake, jumping into this. Paging Jin and Priya. Who's on-call infra?
Jin S: oncall SRE here. seeing queue rise from ~400 -> 2.6k in 12m. p95 moved 1.6s -> 9s, p99 climbing. Worker pods healthy but new workers not being created; provisioner logs show repeated 429s from cloud provider API: "RateLimitExceeded: Too many GPU create calls" and some quota errors mixed in.
Priya K (Infra): confirmed. Cloud console shows both quota saturation for NVIDIA A100s in region and a provider-side rate limit throttling our create calls. Autoscaler is retrying but being rate-limited.
Omar V (Provisioner): autoscaler has exponential backoff but backlog outruns retries. Also noticed we had a spike of cold sessions requiring KV cache warmups causing head-of-line delays.
Tess (Support): we've got 3 customers filing 504s via status page, two with heavy streaming generation (gen-chat, customer tokens). CS escalations landing.
Maya R: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) apply emergency traffic shaping to favor SLA customers; 2) route low-priority chat/generation to quantized-fallback pool; 3) reduce provisioning call rate (batch creates) and attempt fallback SKUs; 4) purge or reschedule low-priority queued jobs. Thoughts?
Jin S: agree. Also we can enable "speculative warm workers" on critical routes (keep a tiny pool warm) to reduce cold-start head-of-line. I'll prepare commands.
Priya K: starting throttling rule for non-SLA routes. Executing admin API:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/edges/rate_limits" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  -d '{"selector":"hosted-api:non-sla","limit_per_min":1200}'
```
Priya K: rate-limit applied. Expect drop in new inflow from noisy tenants within 1m.
Maya R: Omar, can you produce a safe traffic-split command for routing to quantized pool so we can stage it? We don't want regressions for gold customers.
Omar V: posting admin command to shift 35% of non-critical traffic to quantized-fallback:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/traffic/split" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  -d '{"selector":"hosted-api","rules":[{"target":"hosted-us-east","pct":70},{"target":"hosted-us-east-quant","pct":30}],"filter":"tags != \"gold\""}'
```
Maya R: applied. Observed immediate reduction in queue growth rate for non-gold routes. p99 for gold routes remained high due to backlog.
Samir (ML Eng): enabling lightweight model proxies (2-bit quantized) for non-critical routes to preserve throughput. Deployed quantized runtime as fallback.
Omar V: attempting to create fallback instances using alternative SKUs (smaller GPUs) with reduced kernel optimization. Send create in small batches to avoid provider rate limits.
```
# create 2 VMs at a time to avoid provider throttling
for i in 1 2 3; do curl -X POST https://cloud.internal/v1/instances -d '{"gpu_sku":"v100-mini","count":2}'; sleep 12; done
```
Priya K: provider still returning intermittent 429s but some fallback instances spun up. Registered 6 fallback workers so far.
Maya R: are we able to drain queue? Any measurable effect?
Jin S: queue peaked 2.6k -> now 1.1k after throttles, traffic split, and initial fallback nodes. p95 down to ~3.8s, p99 ~11s. Still above normal but improving.
Tess (Support): notifying impacted customers: "We're mitigating high latency by routing lower-priority work to fallback faster paths and spinning fallback capacity. You may see degraded latency for non-critical requests. We'll follow up with detailed RCA."
Samir: launching prefix/KV eviction adjustments to speed warmups. Pushing config: set kv_cache.eviction_policy=aggressive and increase cache-ttl to reduce repeated warms.
Omar V: changed autoscaler config to reduce provisioner API burstiness and added jitter. Also toggled a new feature flag allow_sku_fallback=true for current incident.
Maya R: key point: autoscaler previously tried to create tens of small workers in parallel causing provider rate limit. Changing to batched creates + SKU fallback is helping.
Priya K: cloud support ticket opened (#CLD-91532) requesting quota increase and asking for rate-limit exception. They responded with tentative approval but no ETA.
Jin S: starting queue purge for very-old low-priority jobs to reduce head-of-line blocking:
```
python3 tools/purge_queue.py --channel hosted-api --max-age 900 --priority low --dry-run=false
```
Jin S: purge removed ~350 stale low-priority items. Queue trend improved.
Maya R: summarizing mitigations used: emergency rate limits, traffic split to quantized pool, batched instance creation, SKU fallback, KV eviction tuning, purge of low-priority queue. Customer impact: multiple customers saw 504s/timeouts for ~20-35 minutes during peak; partial recovery after fallbacks.
Tess: CSMs asked for an ETA on full recovery so they can inform customers. Can we estimate?
Jin S: with current fallback nodes and throttles we expect steady drain and normal p95/p99 in 25-45 minutes, assuming provider rate-limits don't reappear.
Maya R: action items: (1) keep batched provisioning and allow_sku_fallback until quota/rate-limit resolved; (2) follow up with cloud for quota and rate-limit exemptions; (3) RFC to make batched-create + SKU-fallback default behavior for autoscaler; (4) postmortem and customer one-pager.
Priya K: creating follow-up tasks and linking to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2759876543. Cloud ticket CLD-91532 created.
Nora (Night Oncall): taking handoff in 45m. I'll monitor the queue and watch for any renewed 429 spikes. acknowledged.
Maya R: handing off to Nora at 2024-03-12T23:13:19Z. If latency spikes, page SRE with pager code. Closing live coordination; migrating notes to incident doc.
incident-bot: status -> mitigated, monitoring. last_action_ts 2759876799
